mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 3% for two consecutive months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to market anticipation of rate hikes.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite inflation above 3% threshold, or the FEDFUNDS rate does not rise in response.

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS rises by more than 10,000 monthly for two consecutive months, labor market strength is interpreted as a positive signal for equity valuations, driving a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Over 1000 test windows, the 20-day forward return is negative when PAYEMS meets the trigger, or the UNRATE remains below 4% during the period.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO below 100 (from 105 to 98) indicates weakening manufacturing capacity, which is expected to depress S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In 5-year rolling windows, no significant negative relationship between INDPRO declines and 60-day forward returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in HOUST above 1300 for three consecutive months signals robust consumer demand, which is associated with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Across 1000 such windows, 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25 percentage points in a single month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to turn negative as investors anticipate tighter credit conditions.
failure_condition: Over 2000 windows, no negative 20-day returns occur after the FEDFUNDS trigger (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in UNRATE and PAYEMS by at least 0.2 percentage points and 5,000 jobs, respectively, indicate labor market resilience and support a 60-day positive S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: In 500 windows, the 60-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in RSAFS below 700,000 suggests reduced corporate liquidity, which is expected to produce a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return in a non-recession regime.
failure_condition: During 1000 such events, the 20-day forward return is not negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in GDPC1 (real GDP) of at least 2% is interpreted as a recession signal, leading to a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: In 2000 such windows, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
